questions.q: In a certain code language, each letter of a word is shifted forward in the alphabet by a number of places equal to its position within the word (the 1st letter shifts by 1 place, the 2nd by 2 places, and so on). What will be the code for the word 'BRICK'?
questions.solution: Shift B by 1, R by 2, I by 3, C by 4 and K by 5. The resulting letters are C,T,L,G,P.

questions.q: Statements: J & K @ L $ M # N Conclusions: I. K @ M II. J # N
options: Both I and II are true
Neither I nor II is true
Either I or II is true
questions.solution: Translate the chain: J≤K>L=M<N. K>M follows directly. J<N is not forced, because J can lie on either side of N.

questions.q: Statements: All doctors are engineers. No engineer is a singer. Some singers are painters. Some painters are engineers. Conclusions: I. No doctor is a singer. II. Some painters are not singers.
questions.solution: Doctors are a subset of engineers, and engineers cannot be singers, so I follows. The painters who are engineers cannot be singers, so II follows.

questions.q: Statements: Some books are pens. All pens are pencils. No pencil is an eraser. Conclusions: I. Some erasers are books. II. No eraser is a book.
questions.solution: The statements do not decide whether any eraser is a book. However, some erasers being books and no eraser being a book are exact complementary possibilities, so either I or II follows.

questions.q: Statements: All cups are plates. Some plates are bowls. No bowl is a spoon. Conclusions: I. Some plates are not spoons. II. No cup is a bowl.
questions.solution: Some plates are bowls, and bowls cannot be spoons. These plates are therefore not spoons. Nothing rules out cups being bowls.

questions.q: In a class of 30 students, Rohit ranks 12th from the top. Priya ranks 8 places below Rohit's rank (counted from the top). If 5 students who rank below Priya leave the class, what will be Priya's new rank from the bottom?
questions.solution: Priya’s top rank is 12+8=20. After five lower-ranked students leave, total size is 25. Her bottom rank is 25−20+1=6.

questions.q: Rohan starts from his office and walks 15m towards East. He then takes a left turn and walks 8m. He again takes a left turn and walks 6m. He then takes a right turn and walks 4m to reach point Z. What is the shortest distance between Rohan's office and point Z, and in which direction does Z lie with respect to the office?
questions.solution: Final displacement is 15−6=9 m east and 8+4=12 m north. Distance = √(9²+12²)=15 m, north-east.
